day.readme: AG-UI is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications. Agents don't fit the request/response model. new.description: A live map beside the chat that shows what Claude Code is doing: tool calls, model steps, hooks, skills and subagents light up as they happen. Local only, in 7 languages.
new.readme: A mod for Claude Code: a live map of the work, in a pane beside the chat. Every tool call, model step, hook and skill sends a pulse from the centre to its station, so you see memory, files, shell, web and agents at work instead of reading a list of commands. It runs on your machine and sends nothing anywhere. Local does not mean blind: like any mod that follows tool calls it is handed each call whole, and it takes names from that and nothing else. What it reads and keeps, and the checks that hold it to that.

new.description: Source-built, locally bound FailSafe distribution of ARTEX (v0.3.15)
new.readme: A source-built, locally bound distribution of ARTEX, an open-source multi-agent security testing harness, with an English interface, a hardened supply chain, and deployment controls. This repository exists because the prebuilt tomicdd/artex Docker image was found to contain an unauthenticated command-execution backdoor in November 2026. new.readme: A Dynamic Island-style component for any React app, installed with shadcn. Show an upload, a timer, a song, a ride on its way, an incoming call or a recording in one island at the top of your app, and shape each activity around your app's own actions. The engine (lib/island/, registry item island-core): the activity stack, four presentations (idle, compact, the split, expanded), springs fitted to frame-by-frame recordings of the real island, long-press, alerts and reduced motion. React only.

threats.title: OpenSSH Password Authentication Bypass on Linux
threats.headline: OpenSSH flaw allows password authentication bypass in some Linux account configurations
threats.summary: OpenSSH on Linux lacks a workaround for a password authentication bypass when musl libc is used without PAM. For some account configurations, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds.
actions: Apply the vendor's fix or mitigations for OpenBSD OpenSSH: CISA lists it as exploited
who: OpenSSH users on Linux with musl libc without PAM
threats.quote: For some configurations of accounts, any password between 256 and 1024 characters succeeds.

gap.method: Lag is how long before the open model's release a closed model first reached the same Capabilities Index score. Today's figure measures from that closed model to today, so it grows until an open model moves the frontier.

hardware.finding: GeForce RTX 5090 decodes fastest; DGX Spark fits the biggest models
hardware.method: Ceiling = memory bandwidth / 16 GB of weights; real decode runs below it. Fits = 80% of memory at 0.55 GB per billion parameters (4-bit). List prices are the maker's own store; street prices are dated checks of a major retailer.

possibilities.title: On-call engineers can question a whole incident's logs in a single context
possibilities.why: Headroom compresses logs and JSON before the model sees them, and Qwen4-Max holds 1 million tokens at $1.50 per million input tokens with measured lower task costs, so an entire incident window can fit cheaply.

possibilities.title: Analysts in regulated firms can query private databases with a 321B-class model on one desk
possibilities.why: The 2.48 bpw quants put a 321B-class MoE on one DGX Spark, datasette-llm can call any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and llama.cpp's new slot scheduler and prompt hashing target exactly this kind of shared local server.

possibilities.title: QA teams can let Codex debug internal staging sites without exposing them
possibilities.why: Chrome DevTools MCP is becoming a standard agent tool for browser debugging, and OpenAI's secure tunnel connects private or localhost MCP servers to Codex without a public endpoint, so a DevTools server inside the network can serve a cloud agent.

possibilities.title: Shared agent skills become dependable team standards once they survive compaction
possibilities.why: Matt Pocock's agent skills show demand for shared skills, and Kiro now reloads requested skills after compaction and lets users set when compaction starts, so a team skill no longer silently drops out of long runs.

possibilities.title: Cloud coding agents can test AWS changes in sandboxes that hold no AWS credentials
possibilities.why: Cline's cloud sandboxes clone a repo and start an agent, and Amazon's CC0 AWS emulator can be baked into that sandbox so the agent exercises cloud code without a real account.
